answer: A bond of 29% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in terrace, and yarrow reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 129 aliases, and each one needs its own funded comet account. That bill is paid per identity, so 201 aliases cost 131 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
